back: Changing raw materials or parts into finished goods, by hand or by machine.
Making huge numbers of identical goods continuously, usually on an assembly line.
Splitting production into separate tasks, each done by different workers who specialise.

front: Name the three processes of manufacturing.

back: Handicraft, job, batch and mass production (also mechanised production).

front: Batch or mass production: what is the difference?
back: Batch makes a set number of one item, then changes; mass makes the same item continuously in huge numbers.
Protects goods, carries information (ingredients, weight, expiry date), helps sell the product.

front: Give three advantages of modern manufacturing.
back: Large output, lower cost per item, standard quality (also exports and specialised skills).

front: Give three disadvantages of modern manufacturing.
back: Job losses, costly machines and dependence on electricity, pollution (also boring work, loss of craft skills).
